requirement: Edition 4 adds new CAS and DTS protocol elements, and robust interoperation with Edition 3 and earlier peers is a key goal.
notes: Basis of decision D6 (Ed3 interop mandatory).

requirement: Determine, for each peer, whether it supports Edition 4 or later.
notes: Three permitted methods follow. Plan 4.4 limits discovery to CAS-1 negotiation.

requirement: Towards a peer that supports only Edition 3, or whose edition cannot be determined, use none of the Edition 4 capabilities.
notes: Text says capabilities "set out in this annex" although this is the main body; see the interp row on that wording.

requirement: Method 1: the edition of a given peer, or of the whole network, may be known a priori.
notes: Permitted source of knowledge. Plan 4.4 chooses CAS-1 negotiation only, so no a priori configuration is offered.

requirement: Method 2: CAS-1 capability negotiation (Annex B) runs for all ARQ data on a node without ALE, so whenever ARQ data flows the peer edition is known.
notes: Our profile has no ALE, so every ARQ soft link negotiates. See B matrix for the procedure.

requirement: With ALE, CAS-1 capability negotiation may be used for ARQ data.
reason: no ALE in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: With ALE, CAS-1 capability negotiation must be used for ARQ data when the peer capability is not known.
reason: no ALE in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Method 3: the CAPABILITY EOW lets a node learn Edition 4 support explicitly without ARQ data, and lets peers learn of an upgrade to Edition 4.
notes: Cited as "Section C.6.4"; the CAPABILITY EOW is C.6.10, EOW type 15 (plan 4.4). Use limited by the interp row below.

requirement: Main 6 offers the CAPABILITY EOW as a way to discover Ed4 peers, but Annex C says Ed4 EOWs shall not be sent to peers whose support is unknown [Ed4 C Table C-4 notes, p.C-67]. Reading: discover editions by CAS-1 negotiation only; send CAPABILITY (and PADDING) only to peers known to be Ed4; non-ARQ traffic to unknown receivers carries no Ed4 EOWs.
notes: Plan 4.4. Conflicting places: Ed4 main 6 p.10; Ed4 C Table C-4 notes p.C-67; Ed4 C PADDING p.C-53.

requirement: Main 6 cites the CAPABILITY EOW as Annex C section C.6.4. Reading: the CAPABILITY EOW is C.6.10, EOW type 15 [Ed4 C p.C-75].
notes: Plan 4.4.

requirement: Main 6 forbids Ed4 capabilities "set out in this annex" but sits in the main body, not an annex. Reading: the rule covers every Edition 4 protocol element in Annexes A, B, C and S that an Edition 3 peer would not understand (Ed4 C_PDUs, D_PDU types 9 to 14, Ed4 EOWs, Ed4-only S_PDU and SIS behaviour on the air).
notes: Editorial wording; not in plan 4.4.

requirement: Profiles are defined for layer services and for applications so a deployment or procurement can state exactly what it needs; waveform and ALE profiles below STANAG 5066 are out of scope.
Table 1 profile option HARD LINKS (Annexes A, B): deprecated, kept only for Edition 3 compatibility.
reason: deprecated option HARD LINKS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Tables 1 and 2)
notes: Plan 4.3: reject the CAS LINK bit with reason 5.

requirement: Table 1 profile option EXPEDITED DATA (Annexes A, C): deprecated, kept only for Edition 3 compatibility.
reason: deprecated option EXPEDITED DATA not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Tables 1 and 2)
notes: Plan 4.3: D_PDU types 4, 5 and 8 are still handled by DTS.

requirement: Table 1 profile option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS (Annexes A, C): service in Annex A, implementation in Annex C, not used by current applications.
reason: option NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Table 1 profile option DUPLEX FIXED (Annexes B, C): duplex operation in a fixed-frequency two-node network.
reason: option DUPLEX FIXED not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Table 1 profile option MULTIPLE ACCESS (Annex B): the Multiple Simultaneous Peer Access model, needed for multicast without ALE in networks of three or more nodes using CSMA or WTRP.
notes: Mandatory in our profile (main Table 2).

requirement: Table 1 profile option ALE 1:1 (Annex B): Single Peer Access with ALE, in mode EXPLICIT CAS-1 or IMPLICIT CAS-1, one of which must be chosen.
reason: option ALE 1:1 not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Table 1 profile option MULTICAST ALE (Annex B): multicast with ALE.
reason: option MULTICAST ALE not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Table 1 profile option DUPLEX WITH ALE (Annexes B, C): duplex with ALE in a multi-node network.
reason: option DUPLEX WITH ALE not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Table 1 profile option HDRCR (Annex C): deprecated High Data Rate Change Request PDU, kept for Edition 3 compatibility.
reason: deprecated option HDRCR not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Tables 1 and 2)

requirement: Table 1 profile option MAC ALE (Annex J): ALE used together with the Annex J MAC.
reason: option MAC ALE not in CSMA Fixed Frequency (main Table 2)

requirement: Annexes A, B, C, D and S are mandatory in every layer services profile.
notes: Annex D: plan 4.3 and 4.4 record our modem-port interpretation; the D matrix carries it.

requirement: Annexes J, K and L are required only by some profiles.
notes: Ours needs J and K, not L.

requirement: If Annex R (routing) or Annex T (TRANSEC) is required, its use must be specified together with the profile.
reason: we implement neither Annex R nor Annex T (plan 4.3)

requirement: Annex R may be used with any profile option.
Annex T is an alternative to Annex D and may become a profile choice in future editions.
Every node in a deployment needs to follow the same layer services profile, because there is no dynamic way to tell profiles apart.
notes: Document as a network-wide setting.

requirement: The NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS option appears in no profile; a future edition may add it.
notes: Contradicted by Table 2, which lists a Non-ARQ Applications profile built on this option; see MAIN-0038.

requirement: Table 2 profile CSMA Fixed Frequency: MULTIPLE ACCESS option plus Annex J and Annex K; multi-node operation under Annex K, suited to light-load surface wave or skywave without ALE.
notes: Our profile (plan 4.1).

requirement: Table 2 profiles other than CSMA Fixed Frequency (ALE Basic implicit and explicit, Duplex Pair, Duplex Network, Multicast ALE Network, Non-ARQ Applications, CSMA with ALE, WTRP Fixed Frequency, WTRP with ALE).
All nodes in a deployment should offer the same applications; the application profile is stated separately from the layer services profile, and both together form a full profile.
The application profile lists at least one application.
notes: First application: HF Operator Chat, Annex O (plan 4.2).

requirement: The listed applications may come from the annexes, from elsewhere, or both.
An application profile that includes Annex Q states whether STANAG 4406 Annex E, RFC 8494 (MULE) or both are supported.
reason: Annex Q not in our application profile (plan 4.2)

requirement: An application profile that includes Annex U states whether IPv4, IPv6 or both are supported.
notes: Applies once the Annex U IP client is added (plan 4.2 later applications).

requirement: Any application that runs over STANAG 5066 may be listed, including HMTP, HFPOP and XMPP (XEP-0365), which Annex F references.

Main 7.2 says NON-ARQ WITH ERRORS is used by no profile [p.12], but Table 2 defines a Non-ARQ Applications profile that mandates it [p.13]. Reading: Table 2 governs; the option belongs to that profile only, and it is outside CSMA Fixed Frequency either way.
notes: Added in review. No effect on our behaviour.

requirement: When a node connects to synchronous serial crypto equipment, the data interface follows Annex D.
reason: no crypto equipment in our deployment (plan 4.3: Annex T and crypto out of scope)

requirement: An application listed in Annex F that is in use binds to its assigned SAP ID; an unused assignment may be reused by a deployment.
notes: see Annex F Table F-1 and plan 10.1
